sentences.zh: 苻洪

translations.literal: Fu Hong
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hong

sentences.zh: 苻洪，字廣世，略陽臨渭氐人也。

translations.literal: Fu Hong, courtesy name Guangshi, was a man of the Di people from Linwei in Lüeyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hong, style Guangshi, was a Di from Linwei in Lüeyang.

sentences.zh: 其先蓋有扈之苗裔，世為西戎酋長。

translations.literal: His ancestors were said to be descendants of Youhu; for generations they had been chieftains among the Western Rong.
translations.idiomatic: The family claimed descent from Youhu; for generations his forebears had been chiefs of the western tribes.

sentences.zh: 始其家池中蒲生，長五丈，五節如竹形，時咸謂之蒲家，因以為氏焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning cattail grew in a pond at his home, five zhang in height, with five joints like bamboo; people at the time all spoke of the Pu household, and on that basis they took Pu as their surname.
translations.idiomatic: Once, cattails sprouted in the family pond—five zhang tall, jointed like bamboo—so folk called them the Pu clan, and the surname Pu stuck.

sentences.zh: 父懷歸，部落小帥。

translations.literal: His father was Huai Gui, a minor commander of the tribe.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Huai Gui, was a petty chieftain among the tribesmen.

sentences.zh: 先是，隴右大雨，百姓苦之，謠曰：「雨若不止，洪水必起。

translations.literal: Before this, there was heavy rain in Longyou; the people suffered, and a song ran: “If the rain does not stop, a great flood is sure to rise.”
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, ceaseless rain had afflicted Longyou, and a ditty warned: if the downpour never ended, a mighty flood would follow.

sentences.zh: 」故因名曰洪。

translations.literal: Therefore on that account he was named Hong.
translations.idiomatic: So the child was given the name Hong.

sentences.zh: 好施，多權略，驍武善騎射。

translations.literal: He loved to give generously, was full of stratagems, fierce in war, and skilled at riding and shooting.
translations.idiomatic: He was open-handed, resourceful, a fierce fighter, and an expert horseman and archer.

sentences.zh: 屬永嘉之亂，乃散千金，召英傑之士訪安危變通之術。

translations.literal: When the Yongjia turmoil struck, he scattered a thousand in gold to summon heroes and consult them on how to secure the realm and adapt to change.
translations.idiomatic: Amid the Yongjia upheaval he spent a fortune to gather bold men and ask how order might be restored.

sentences.zh: 宗人蒲光、蒲突遂推洪為盟主。

translations.literal: His clansmen Pu Guang and Pu Tu thereupon urged Hong to be covenant lord.
translations.idiomatic: Clansmen Pu Guang and Pu Tu then made him head of the league.

sentences.zh: 劉曜僭號長安，光等逼洪歸曜，拜率義侯。

translations.literal: Liu Yao assumed imperial title at Chang’an; Guang and others forced Hong to submit to Yao, who appointed him Marquis Who Leads Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yao declared himself emperor at Chang’an, Guang and the rest pressed Hong to join him; Yao enfeoffed him as Marquis Who Leads the Righteous.

sentences.zh: 曜敗，洪西保隴山。

translations.literal: When Yao was defeated, Hong withdrew west and held Long Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: After Yao’s defeat, Hong fell back west and fortified the Long range.

sentences.zh: 石季龍將攻上邽，洪又請降。

translations.literal: Shi Hu was about to attack Shanggui, and Hong again begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: As Shi Hu prepared to strike Shanggui, Hong once more offered submission.

sentences.zh: 季龍大悅，拜冠軍將軍，委以西方之事。

translations.literal: Shi Hu was greatly pleased, appointed him General Who Uplifts the Army, and entrusted him with affairs in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu was delighted, named him General Who Champions the Army, and put the western theater in his hands.

sentences.zh: 季龍滅石生，洪說季龍宜徙關中豪傑及羌戎內實京師。

translations.literal: When Shi Hu destroyed Shi Sheng, Hong urged Shi Hu that he ought to relocate the notables of Guanzhong and the Qiang and Rong inward to strengthen the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Hu eliminated Shi Sheng, Hong advised moving Guanzhong’s elite and the Qiang and Rong peoples into the heartland to fill out the capital.

sentences.zh: 季龍從之，以洪為龍驤將軍、流人都督，處於枋頭。

translations.literal: Shi Hu followed this, appointed Hong as General of the Soaring Dragon and Area Commander of the Displaced Populations, and stationed him at Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu agreed, made Hong General of the Soaring Dragon and Area Commander over the displaced populations, and based him at Fangtou.

sentences.zh: 累有戰功，封西平郡公，其部下賜爵關內侯者二千餘人，以洪為關內領侯將。

translations.literal: He repeatedly earned battle honors, was enfeoffed Duke of Xiping, more than two thousand of his followers were granted the rank of marquis within the passes, and Hong was appointed General Who Commands the Marquises Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Battle honors piled up: he became Duke of Xiping, over two thousand of his men received “marquis within the passes,” and Hong was named to lead those titled marquises.

sentences.zh: 冉閔言于季龍曰：「苻洪雄果，其諸子並非常才，宜密除之。

translations.literal: Ran Min said to Shi Hu: “Fu Hong is bold and capable; his sons are all extraordinary talents—you ought secretly to eliminate them.”
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min warned Shi Hu: “Fu Hong is fierce and able, and his sons are no ordinary men; cut them down before they grow dangerous.”

sentences.zh: 」季龍待之愈厚。

translations.literal: Shi Hu treated Hong even more generously.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu showered Hong with even greater favor instead.

sentences.zh: 及石遵即位，閔又以為言，遵乃去洪都督，余如前。

translations.literal: When Shi Zun ascended the throne, Min spoke again; Zun then removed Hong’s area command, but everything else stayed as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Zun took the throne, Ran Min repeated the warning; Zun stripped Hong of his area command but left his other posts intact.

sentences.zh: 洪怨之，乃遣使降晉。

translations.literal: Hong resented this and sent envoys to surrender to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Smarting at the slight, Hong dispatched envoys to offer allegiance to Jin.

sentences.zh: 後石鑒殺遵，所在兵起，洪有眾十餘萬。

translations.literal: Later Shi Jian killed Shi Zun; troops rose everywhere, and Hong commanded more than a hundred thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Jian murdered Shi Zun, rebellion flared across the land, and Hong’s following passed a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: ，帝以洪為征北大將軍、都督河北諸軍事、冀州刺史、廣川郡公。

translations.literal: The Jin emperor thereupon appointed Hong General Who Conquers the North, Area Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs north of the Yellow River, Governor of Ji Province, and Duke of Guangchuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin court then invested him as General Who Conquers the North, commander of Hebei’s armies, Governor of Ji, and Duke of Guangchuan.

sentences.zh: 時有說洪稱尊號者，洪亦以讖文有「草付應王」，又其孫堅背有「草付」字，遂改姓苻氏，自稱大將軍、大單于、三秦王。

translations.literal: Some urged Hong to assume the supreme title; Hong also because a prophecy read “grass-payment shall answer as king,” and moreover his grandson Jian bore on his back the characters “grass-payment,” changed his surname to Fu, and styled himself Grand General, Great Chanyu, and King of the Three Qins.
translations.idiomatic: Counselors pressed him to take the throne; a prophecy spoke of the “grass-Fu” claimant, and his grandson Jian had those graphs inked on his back—so he adopted the surname Fu and proclaimed himself Grand General, Great Chanyu, and King of the Three Qins.

sentences.zh: 洪謂博士胡文曰：「孤率眾十萬，居形勝之地，冉閔、慕容俊可指辰而殄，姚襄父子克之在吾數中，孤取天下，有易於漢祖。

translations.literal: Hong said to the erudite Hu Wen: “I lead a hundred thousand men and hold commanding ground; Ran Min and Murong Jun can be wiped out by a set hour; Yao Xiang father and son are already in my reckoning; for me to take the realm is easier than it was for the Han founder.”
translations.idiomatic: Hong told Academician Hu Wen: “I command a hundred thousand soldiers on decisive terrain; Ran Min and Murong Jun I can crush at a stroke; the Yao Xiang pair are already counted; seizing the empire will be easier for me than it was for Han Gaozu.”

sentences.zh: 」初，季龍以麻秋鎮枹罕，冉閔之亂，秋歸鄴，洪使子雄擊而獲之，以秋為軍師將軍。

translations.literal: At first Shi Hu had stationed Ma Qiu at Baohan; during Ran Min’s rebellion Qiu returned to Ye; Hong sent his son Xiong to attack and capture him, and appointed Qiu General Who Directs the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Shi Hu had garrisoned Ma Qiu at Baohan; when Ran Min rose, Qiu fled to Ye, where Hong’s son Xiong seized him and Hong named him Director of the Army.

sentences.zh: 秋說洪西都長安，洪深然之。

translations.literal: Ma Qiu urged Hong to make his western capital Chang’an; Hong strongly agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qiu argued for shifting the capital west to Chang’an, and Hong heartily concurred.

sentences.zh: 既而秋因宴鴆洪，將並其眾，世子健收而斬之。

translations.literal: Before long Qiu poisoned Hong with wine at a banquet, intending to swallow his army; the heir Jian seized him and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Qiu poisoned Hong at a feast to seize his host; Crown Prince Jian arrested and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 洪將死，謂健曰：「所以未入關者，言中州可指時而定。

translations.literal: When Hong was dying he said to Jian: “The reason I had not yet entered the pass was that I believed the Central Plain could be settled in short order.”
translations.idiomatic: Dying, Hong told Jian: “I stayed out of the passes only because I thought the heartland could be taken quickly.”

sentences.zh: 今見困豎子，中原非汝兄弟所能辦。

translations.literal: “Now I am trapped by a stripling; the Central Plain is not something you brothers can handle.”
translations.idiomatic: “Now a wretch has undone me; you brothers cannot finish the work in the plain.”

sentences.zh: 關中形勝，吾亡後便可鼓行而西。

translations.literal: “Guanzhong is strategically decisive; after my death you may beat the drums and march west.”
translations.idiomatic: “Guanzhong is the ground that decides victory—when I am gone, strike west without delay.”

sentences.zh: 」言終而死，年六十六。

translations.literal: With these words he died, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He finished speaking and died at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 健僭位，偽諡惠武帝。

translations.literal: When Jian usurped the throne he posthumously titled him with the false posthumous name Emperor Huiwu.
translations.idiomatic: After Jian took power he gave Hong the spurious posthumous title Emperor Huiwu.

sentences.zh: 苻健

translations.literal: Fu Jian
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian

sentences.zh: 苻健，字建業，洪第三子也。

translations.literal: Fu Jian, courtesy name Jianye, was Hong’s third son.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian, style Jianye, was the third son of Fu Hong.

sentences.zh: 初，母薑氏夢大羆而孕之，及長，勇果便弓馬，好施，善事人，甚為石季龍父子所親愛。

translations.literal: At first his mother Lady Jiang dreamed of a great bear and conceived him; grown, he was brave and decisive, handy with bow and horse, loved to give generously, was skilled at dealing with people, and was much favored by Shi Hu and his son.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Jiang dreamed of a great bear before his birth; as a man he was bold, skilled with bow and horse, generous, and winning in manner—Shi Hu and his heir doted on him.

sentences.zh: 季龍雖外禮苻氏，心實忌之，乃陰殺其諸兄，而不害健也。

translations.literal: Though Shi Hu outwardly treated the Fu with courtesy, in his heart he envied them; he secretly killed Hong’s elder sons but did not harm Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu’s courtesy toward the Fu masked suspicion; he murdered Hong’s older sons in secret but spared Jian.

sentences.zh: 及洪死，健嗣位，去秦王之號，稱晉爵，遣使告喪于京師，且聽王命。

translations.literal: When Hong died, Jian succeeded, set aside the title King of Qin, assumed Jin noble rank, sent envoys to announce mourning at the capital, and declared obedience to imperial orders.
translations.idiomatic: On Hong’s death Jian took his place, dropped the “King of Qin” style, accepted Jin’s noble titles, reported the funeral to the southern court, and professed loyalty.

sentences.zh: 時京兆杜洪竊據長安，自稱晉征北將軍、雍州刺史，戎夏多歸之。

translations.literal: At that time Du Hong of Jingzhao had seized Chang’an, styled himself Jin’s General Who Conquers the North and Governor of Yong Province, and many from both Hu and Han submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong of Jingzhao held Chang’an, calling himself Jin’s northern commander and Governor of Yong, and drew large followings from Hu and Han alike.

sentences.zh: 健密圖關中，懼洪知之，乃偽受石祗官，繕宮室於枋頭，課所部種麥，示無西意，有知而不種者，健殺之以徇。

translations.literal: Jian secretly plotted for Guanzhong and feared Du Hong would learn of it; he falsely accepted office from Shi Zhi, repaired palaces at Fangtou, and ordered his men to sow wheat to show no western ambition—whoever knew and refused to plant, Jian executed as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Jian meant to take Guanzhong but hid it from Du Hong: he took a sham post from Shi Zhi, built at Fangtou, and forced everyone to plant wheat as proof he would not march west—slackers were executed pour encourager les autres.

sentences.zh: 既而自稱晉征西大將軍、都督關中諸軍事、雍州刺史，盡眾西行，起浮橋於盟津以濟。

translations.literal: Then he styled himself Jin’s Grand General Who Conquers the West, Area Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Guanzhong, Governor of Yong Province, marched his whole host west, and threw a floating bridge across at Meng Ford to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Then he declared himself Jin’s Grand General Who Conquers the West, commander of Guanzhong, Governor of Yong, and drove the entire army west, spanning the river at Meng Ford.

sentences.zh: 遣其弟雄率步騎五千入潼關，兄子菁自軹關入河東。

translations.literal: He sent his younger brother Xiong with five thousand foot and horse through Tong Pass, and his nephew Jing from Zhi Pass into Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xiong with five thousand men through Tong Pass and his nephew Jing from Zhi Pass into Hedong.

sentences.zh: 健執菁手曰：「事若不捷，汝死河北，我死河南，不及黃泉，無相見也。

translations.literal: Jian took Jing’s hand and said: “If we fail, you die north of the river and I south of it; before we reach the Yellow Springs we shall not meet.”
translations.idiomatic: Clasping Jing’s hand he vowed: “If this miscarries, you perish north of the Yellow River and I south of it—we meet again only in the underworld.”

sentences.zh: 」既濟，焚橋，自統大眾繼雄而進。

translations.literal: Once across he burned the bridge and led the main army after Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing he burned the bridge and followed Xiong with the main force.

sentences.zh: 杜洪遣其將張先要健於潼關，健逆擊破之。

translations.literal: Du Hong sent his general Zhang Xian to intercept Jian at Tong Pass; Jian struck back and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong’s general Zhang Xian tried to stop Jian at Tong Pass; Jian turned and routed him.

sentences.zh: 健雖戰勝，猶修箋于洪，並送名馬珍寶，請至長安上尊號。

translations.literal: Though Jian had won, he still wrote to Du Hong and sent famous horses and treasures, inviting him to Chang’an to receive a loftier title.
translations.idiomatic: Even in victory Jian wrote Du Hong, sending fine horses and jewels and inviting him to Chang’an for a grander investiture.

sentences.zh: 洪曰：「幣重言甘，誘我也。

translations.literal: Du Hong said: “Rich gifts and honeyed words—this is to lure me.”
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong replied: “Heavy bribes and sweet words mean a trap.”

sentences.zh: 」乃盡召關中之眾來距。

translations.literal: He then summoned all the hosts of Guanzhong to resist.
translations.idiomatic: He called up every force in Guanzhong to oppose Jian.

sentences.zh: 健筮之，遇《泰》之《臨》，健曰：「小往大來，吉亨。

translations.literal: Jian cast the yarrow and drew Hexagram Tai changing to Lin; Jian said: “The small departs and the great arrives—auspicious and penetrating.”
translations.idiomatic: Jian divined and got Tai moving to Lin: “The small goes out, the great comes in—auspicious success.”

sentences.zh: 昔往東而小，今還西而大，吉孰大焉！

translations.literal: “Formerly we went east and were small; now we return west and are great—what omen could be greater!”
translations.idiomatic: “Once we marched east as the lesser power; now we return west as the greater—what sign could top that?”

sentences.zh: 」是時眾星夾河西流，占者以為百姓還西之象。

translations.literal: At that time many stars flanked the River and seemed to flow west; diviners read it as a sign that the people would return west.
translations.idiomatic: Stars clustered along the river and seemed to drift westward; soothsayers called it a portent of folk returning to the western heartland.

sentences.zh: 健遂進軍，次赤水，遣雄略地渭北，又敗張先于陰槃，擒之，諸城盡陷，菁所至無不降者，三輔略定。

translations.literal: Jian advanced, halted at Chishui, sent Xiong to sweep the north bank of the Wei, again defeated Zhang Xian at Yinpan and captured him; the cities fell in turn; wherever Jing went there was surrender; the Three Adjuncts were largely settled.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed on to Chishui, sent Xiong to clear the Wei’s north shore, crushed Zhang Xian again at Yinpan and took him; city after city opened; Jing’s column met no resistance; the Three Adjuncts were nearly his.

sentences.zh: 健引兵至長安，洪奔司竹。

translations.literal: Jian led his troops to Chang’an; Du Hong fled to Sizhu.
translations.idiomatic: Jian closed on Chang’an while Du Hong bolted for the bamboo groves at Sizhu.

sentences.zh: 健入而都之，遣使獻捷京師，並修好于桓溫。

translations.literal: Jian entered and made it his capital, sent messengers to report victory to the southern court, and opened cordial relations with Huan Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He occupied the city as his capital, reported triumph to Jiankang, and courted Huan Wen’s goodwill.

sentences.zh: 健軍師將軍賈玄碩等表健為侍中、大都督關中諸軍事、大單于、秦王，健怒曰：「我官位輕重，非若等所知。

translations.literal: Jian’s military director Jia Xuanshuo and others memorialized that Jian be made Palace Attendant, Area Commander-in-Chief of Guanzhong, Great Chanyu, and King of Qin; Jian angrily said: “The weight of my offices is not for you to judge.”
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xuanshuo and staff asked that Jian be named palace attendant, Guanzhong commander, Great Chanyu, and King of Qin; Jian snapped that such rank was none of their business.

sentences.zh: 」既而潛使諷玄碩等使上尊號。

translations.literal: Shortly after he secretly sent agents to prompt Xuanshuo and the others to urge a more exalted title on him.
translations.idiomatic: He then quietly had the same men coached to press him toward the throne.

sentences.zh: ，僭稱天王、大單于，赦境內死罪，建元皇始，繕宗廟社稷，置百官于長安。

translations.literal: He then usurped the titles King of Heaven and Great Chanyu, granted amnesty for capital crimes within his realm, established the era name Huangshi, repaired the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain, and installed the full bureaucracy at Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed himself Heavenly King and Great Chanyu, amnestied capital crimes, adopted the reign name Huangshi, rebuilt the temples and altars, and seated a full administration at Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 立妻強氏為天王皇后，子萇為天王皇太子，弟雄為丞相、都督中外諸軍事、車騎大將軍、領雍州刺史，自余封授各有差。

translations.literal: He established his wife Lady Qiang as queen of the Heavenly King, his son Chang as crown prince, his brother Xiong as chancellor, Area Commander-in-Chief of court and field, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and concurrent Governor of Yong Province; others received graded appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Qiang became queen; Crown Prince Chang succeeded in line; Xiong became chancellor, supreme commander, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Governor of Yong; the rest took posts by rank.

sentences.zh: 初，杜洪之奔也，招晉梁州刺史司馬勳。

translations.literal: At first, when Du Hong had fled, he had summoned Jin’s Governor of Liang Province Sima Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Du Hong’s flight had prompted him to call in Jin’s Liang governor Sima Xun.

sentences.zh: 至是，勳率步騎三萬入秦川，健敗之于五丈原。

translations.literal: By now Xun led thirty thousand foot and horse into Qinchuan; Jian defeated him at Wuzhangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Now Xun marched thirty thousand men into Qinchuan; Jian broke him at Wuzhangyuan.

sentences.zh: 八年，健僭即皇帝位於太極前殿，諸公進為王，以大單于授其子萇。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Jian usurped the imperial throne in the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate; the dukes were promoted to kings, and the Great Chanyu title went to his son Chang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he took the imperial seat in the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate, raised his dukes to kings, and passed the Great Chanyu title to Chang.

sentences.zh: 杜洪屯宜秋，為其將張琚所殺，琚自立為秦王，置百官。

translations.literal: Du Hong garrisoned Yiqiu, was killed by his general Zhang Ju, who declared himself King of Qin and set up officials.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong camped at Yiqiu until his general Zhang Ju slew him, styled himself King of Qin, and appointed a court.

sentences.zh: 健率步騎二萬攻琚，斬其首。

translations.literal: Jian led twenty thousand foot and horse against Zhang Ju and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian marched twenty thousand men against Zhang Ju and struck off his head.

sentences.zh: 健至自宜秋，遣雄、菁率眾掠關東，並援石季龍豫州刺史張遇于許昌，與晉鎮西將軍謝尚戰于潁水之上，王師敗績。

translations.literal: Jian returned from Yiqiu, sent Xiong and Jing east of the pass to raid and to relieve Shi Hu’s Governor of Yu Province Zhang Yu at Xuchang; they fought Jin’s General Who Guards the West Xie Shang on the Ying River, and the imperial army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from Yiqiu, he sent Xiong and Jing to scour the east and aid Zhang Yu, Shi Hu’s man at Xuchang; they met Xie Shang on the Ying and shattered the Jin force.

sentences.zh: 雄乘勝逐北，至於壘門，殺傷太半，遂虜遇及其眾歸於長安，拜遇司空、豫州刺史，鎮許昌。

translations.literal: Xiong pressed the pursuit to the camp gates, killing and wounding more than half, captured Zhang Yu and his following, brought them to Chang’an, appointed Yu Minister of Works and Governor of Yu Province, and stationed him at Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong chased the broken army to its gates, slaughtered half or more, dragged Zhang Yu and his troops to Chang’an, named Yu minister and governor, and left him holding Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 雄攻王擢於隴上，擢奔涼州，雄屯隴東。

translations.literal: Xiong attacked Wang Zhuo on Long; Zhuo fled to Liangzhou; Xiong camped east of Long.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong struck Wang Zhuo on the Long plateau; Zhuo ran to Liangzhou; Xiong halted east of Long.

sentences.zh: 張重華拜擢征東大將軍，使與其將張弘、宋修連兵伐雄。

translations.literal: Zhang Chonghua appointed Zhuo General Who Conquers the East and had him join Zhang Hong and Song Xiu in a joint campaign against Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua made Zhuo eastern commander and teamed him with Zhang Hong and Song Xiu against Xiong.

sentences.zh: 雄與菁率眾擊敗之，獲弘、修送長安。

translations.literal: Xiong and Jing led the host to defeat them, captured Hong and Song, and sent them to Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong and Jing crushed the allied force, took Hong and Song prisoner, and shipped them to Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 初，張遇自許昌來降，健納遇後母韓氏為昭儀，每於眾中謂遇曰：「卿，吾子也。

translations.literal: At first, when Zhang Yu had surrendered from Xuchang, Jian had taken Yu’s stepmother Lady Han as an honored concubine and often said in public: “You are my son.”
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yu first defected from Xuchang, Jian had installed Yu’s stepmother Lady Han as concubine and humiliated Yu by calling him “my son” before the court.

sentences.zh: 」遇慚恨，引關中諸將欲以雍州歸順，乃與健中黃門劉晃謀夜襲健，事覺，遇害。

translations.literal: Yu was ashamed and resentful; he drew in the Guanzhong generals intending to hand Yong Province to Jin, and plotted with palace attendant Liu Huang to strike Jian by night; the plot leaked and Yu was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Burning with shame, Yu rallied Guanzhong’s commanders to deliver Yong to Jin and conspired with Liu Huang to ambush Jian; the scheme surfaced and Yu died for it.

sentences.zh: 於是孔特起池陽，劉珍、夏侯顯起鄠，喬景起雍，胡陽赤起司竹，呼延毒起霸城，眾數萬人，並遣使詣征西桓溫、中軍殷浩請救。

translations.literal: Thereupon Kong Te rose at Chiyang, Liu Zhen and Xia Houqi at Hu, Qiao Jing at Yong, Hu Yangchi at Sizhu, Huyandu at Bashicheng—each with tens of thousands—and all sent envoys to General Who Conquers the West Huan Wen and Central Army commander Yin Hao begging rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Revolt flared: Kong Te at Chiyang, Liu Zhen and Xia Houqi at Hu, Qiao Jing at Yong, Hu Yangchi at Sizhu, Huyandu at Bashicheng—each mustered tens of thousands—and all begged Huan Wen and Yin Hao for relief.

sentences.zh: 雄遣菁掠上洛郡，于豐陽縣立荊州，以引南金奇貨、弓竿漆蠟，通關市，來遠商，於是國用充足，而異賄盈積矣。

translations.literal: Xiong sent Jing to raid Shangluo commandery, founded a Jing Province at Fengyang county to channel southern gold, curios, bows, lacquer, and wax, opened border markets and lured distant traders, so state coffers filled and exotic goods piled high.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong had Jing plunder Shangluo and set up a shadow “Jing Province” at Fengyang to funnel southern bullion, luxuries, bows, lacquer, and beeswax; frontier trade boomed and the treasury overflowed.

sentences.zh: 十年，溫率眾四萬趨長安，遣別將入淅川，攻上洛，執健荊州刺史郭敬，而遣司馬勳掠西鄙。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Wen led forty thousand men toward Chang’an, sent a column into the Xi valley, took Shangluo, captured Jian’s Governor of Jing Province Guo Jing, and had Sima Xun ravage the western marches.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Huan Wen drove forty thousand men on Chang’an, detached a force up the Xi to seize Shangluo and Fu Jian’s governor Guo Jing, and ordered Sima Xun to scour the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 健遣其子萇率雄、菁等眾五萬，距溫于堯柳城、愁思堆。

translations.literal: Jian sent his son Chang with Xiong, Jing, and others—fifty thousand men—to oppose Wen at Yaoliu city and Chousidui.
translations.idiomatic: Jian answered with fifty thousand under Chang, Xiong, and Jing, blocking Huan Wen at Yaoliu and Chousidui.

sentences.zh: 溫轉戰而前，次於灞上，萇等退營城南。

translations.literal: Wen fought forward and halted at Bashang; Chang and the others drew their camp south of the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen fought through to Bashang; Chang’s corps fell back south of the city.

sentences.zh: 健以羸兵六千固守長安小城，遣精銳三萬為遊軍以距溫。

translations.literal: Jian held Chang’an’s inner town with six thousand worn troops and sent thirty thousand elites as a mobile corps against Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Jian defended the lesser city of Chang’an with six thousand threadbare soldiers while thirty thousand picked troops harried Wen in the field.

sentences.zh: 三輔郡縣多降于溫。

translations.literal: Many commanderies and counties of the Three Adjuncts surrendered to Wen.
translations.idiomatic: County after county in the Three Adjuncts went over to Huan Wen.

sentences.zh: 健別使雄領騎七千，與桓沖戰于白鹿原，王師敗績，又破司馬勳于子午穀。

translations.literal: Jian separately had Xiong lead seven thousand horse to fight Huan Chong at Bailuyuan; the imperial army was routed; he also broke Sima Xun in Zigug valley.
translations.idiomatic: He detached Xiong with seven thousand cavalry to meet Huan Chong on Bailuyuan and shattered the Jin horse; Sima Xun was beaten again in Zigug.

sentences.zh: 初，健聞溫之來也，收麥清野以待之，故溫眾大饑。

translations.literal: At first, hearing Wen was coming, Jian had the wheat gathered and the countryside stripped to starve him.
translations.idiomatic: Forewarned of Huan Wen’s march, Jian had stripped the fields and barns so the invaders would go hungry.

sentences.zh: 至是，徙關中三千餘戶而歸。

translations.literal: By then Wen moved more than three thousand households out of Guanzhong and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen then deported three thousand-odd households from Guanzhong and retreated.

sentences.zh: 及至潼關，又為萇等所敗，司馬勳奔還漢中。

translations.literal: When he reached Tong Pass he was again defeated by Chang and others; Sima Xun fled back to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: At Tong Pass Chang struck him again; Sima Xun bolted for Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 其年，西虜乞沒軍邪遣子入侍，健於是置來賓館于平朔門以懷遠人。

translations.literal: That year the western tribesman Qimojunxie sent his son as hostage; Jian built the Guest Reception Lodge at Pingpuo Gate to court those from afar.
translations.idiomatic: The same year the western leader Qimojunxie sent a son as hostage, and Jian opened a state guesthouse at Pingpuo Gate to impress distant peoples.

sentences.zh: 起靈台于杜門。

translations.literal: He raised a spirit terrace at Dumen.
translations.idiomatic: He erected a spirit terrace at Dumen.

sentences.zh: 與百姓約法三章，薄賦卑宮，垂心政事，優禮耆老，修尚儒學，而關右稱來蘇焉。

translations.literal: With the people he agreed on a three-article law, kept taxes light and palaces modest, gave his heart to government, honored elders, and promoted Confucian learning; west of the pass they said he had brought them renewal.
translations.idiomatic: He pledged the three simple laws, kept levies low and building modest, worked at governance, favored graybeards, and patronized Confucian schools—west of the pass they compared him to the “coming in renewal” of the Shang restoration.

sentences.zh: 新平有長人見，語百姓張靖曰：「苻氏應天受命，今當太平，外面者歸中而安泰。

translations.literal: In Xinping a very tall man appeared, told the commoner Zhang Jing: “The Fu are to receive Heaven’s mandate; peace is at hand; those outside will return within and find calm.”
translations.idiomatic: At Xinping a giant figure told the commoner Zhang Jing that the Fu would take the mandate, peace would follow, and wanderers would come home to rest.

sentences.zh: 」問姓名，弗答，俄而不見。

translations.literal: When asked his name he gave none, then suddenly vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Asked his name, he gave none and vanished.

sentences.zh: 新平令以聞，健以為妖，下靖獄。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Xinping reported it; Jian judged it sorcery and jailed Zhang Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The county magistrate reported the tale; Jian called it witchcraft and imprisoned Zhang Jing.

sentences.zh: 會大雨霖，河、渭溢，蒲津監冠登得一屐於河，長七盡三寸，人跡稱之，指長尺餘，文深一寸。

translations.literal: Then came weeks of rain; the Yellow and Wei rivers flooded; Guan Deng, inspector at Pujin, found in the river a shoe seven chi and three cun long—the footprint matched it, toes over a chi long, the impression one cun deep.
translations.idiomatic: Relentless storms swelled the Yellow and Wei; Guan Deng, warden of Pujin ford, pulled from the current a sandal some seven chi and three cun long—its tread matched a foot with toes over a chi long and an imprint a cun deep.

sentences.zh: 健歎曰：「覆載之中何所不有，張靖所見定不虛也。

translations.literal: Jian sighed: “Between heaven and earth what is there not? Zhang Jing’s vision was no empty tale.”
translations.idiomatic: Jian mused: “The world holds stranger things than we know—Zhang Jing’s vision must be true.”

sentences.zh: 」赦之。

translations.literal: He pardoned Zhang Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He freed Zhang Jing.

sentences.zh: 蝗蟲大起，自華澤至隴山，食百草無遺。

translations.literal: Locusts rose in vast numbers from Huaze to Long Mountain and devoured every plant.
translations.idiomatic: Swarms of locusts swept from Huaze to Long, stripping every green thing.

sentences.zh: 牛馬相噉毛，猛獸及狼食人，行路斷絕。

translations.literal: Cattle and horses gnawed each other’s hides; wolves and beasts ate travelers; roads were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Horses and oxes chewed one another’s coats; wolves and brutes preyed on men; highways went dead.

sentences.zh: 健自蠲百姓租稅，減膳撤懸，素服避正殿。

translations.literal: Jian remitted commoners’ rent and taxes, reduced palace meals and silenced the bells, wore undyed robes, and avoided the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: Jian cancelled taxes, cut court feasts and music, dressed in white, and quit the main hall.

sentences.zh: 初，桓溫之入關也，其太子萇與溫戰，為流矢所中死。

translations.literal: At first, when Huan Wen entered the pass, Crown Prince Chang had fought him and died of a stray arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Crown Prince Chang had faced Huan Wen’s invasion and fallen to a stray shaft.

sentences.zh: 至是，立其子生為太子。

translations.literal: Thereupon he established Chang’s son Sheng as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He then named Chang’s son Sheng heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 健寢疾，菁勒兵入東宮，將殺苻生自立。

translations.literal: Jian fell gravely ill; Jing led troops into the Eastern Palace to kill Fu Sheng and seize the throne.
translations.idiomatic: As Jian sickened, Jing marched on the Eastern Palace intending to murder Fu Sheng and usurp.

sentences.zh: 時生侍健疾，菁以健為死，回攻東掖門。

translations.literal: At the time Sheng was nursing Jian’s illness; Jing thought Jian dead, wheeled about, and assaulted the east-side gate.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was at Jian’s bedside; Jing, believing the king already dead, turned his column against the east inner gate.

sentences.zh: 健聞變，升端門陳兵，眾皆舍杖逃散，執菁殺之。

translations.literal: Hearing of the coup, Jian mounted the Duan Gate, drew up troops; the mutineers threw down arms and fled; he seized Jing and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, hearing the uproar, took the Duan Gate with guards; the rebels dropped their weapons and scattered; Jing was caught and killed.

sentences.zh: 數日，健死，時年三十九，在位四年。

translations.literal: Several days later Jian died, aged thirty-nine, having reigned four years.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Jian died at thirty-nine after four years on the throne.

sentences.zh: 偽諡明皇帝，廟號世宗，後改曰高祖。

translations.literal: He received the false posthumous title Emperor Ming, temple name Shizong; later this was changed to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously styled Emperor Ming with temple Shizong, later renamed Gaozu.

translations.literal: A horizontal rule in the original table layout (Wikisource).
translations.idiomatic: The source edition marks this break with a ruled line.

sentences.zh: 健第三子 生

translations.literal: Jian’s third son: Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng—Fu Jian’s third son.

translations.literal: A horizontal rule in the original table layout (Wikisource).
translations.idiomatic: Another typographic rule follows the heading.

sentences.zh: 生字長生，健第三子也。

translations.literal: Sheng’s courtesy name was Changsheng; he was Jian’s third son.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng, style Changsheng, was the third son of Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 幼而無賴，祖洪甚惡之。

translations.literal: In youth he was a scoundrel; his grandfather Hong detested him.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was a bully, and his grandfather Fu Hong loathed him.

sentences.zh: 生無一目，為兒童時，洪戲之，問侍者曰：「吾聞瞎兒一淚，信乎？

translations.literal: Sheng had only one eye; when still a child, Hong teased him and asked an attendant: “I have heard that a one-eyed boy has but one tear—is that true?”
translations.idiomatic: Born with a single eye, he was mocked in childhood when Fu Hong asked a servant whether a one-eyed child truly shed only one tear.

sentences.zh: 」侍者曰：「然。

translations.literal: The attendant said: “It is so.”
translations.idiomatic: The servant answered that it was.

sentences.zh: 」生怒，引佩刀自刺出血，曰：「此亦一淚也。

translations.literal: Sheng grew angry, drew his girdle knife and stabbed himself until blood flowed, saying: “This too is a tear.”
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, he drew his belt knife, cut himself until he bled, and snapped, “There—another tear.”

sentences.zh: 」洪大驚，鞭之。

translations.literal: Hong was greatly startled and flogged him.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was horrified and had him whipped.

sentences.zh: 生曰：「性耐刀槊，不堪鞭捶。

translations.literal: Sheng said: “By nature I can endure blades and spears; I cannot bear flogging.”
translations.idiomatic: He retorted that blades and spears he could stand, but not the rod.

sentences.zh: 」洪曰：「汝為爾不已，吾將以汝為奴。

translations.literal: Hong said: “If you keep on like this, I will make you a slave.”
translations.idiomatic: Hong threatened to reduce him to slavery if he did not mend his ways.

sentences.zh: 」生曰：「可不如石勒也。

translations.literal: Sheng said: “That would still be better than Shi Le.”
translations.idiomatic: He sneered that even slavery would beat being another Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 」洪懼，跣而掩其口，謂健曰：「此兒狂勃，宜早除之，不然，長大必破人家。

translations.literal: Hong feared this, went barefoot and covered his mouth, and said to Jian: “This boy is violent and wild; you should eliminate him early; otherwise, grown, he will ruin a household.”
translations.idiomatic: Hong blanched, clapped a hand over his mouth, and warned Fu Jian to kill the boy before his savagery destroyed the clan.

sentences.zh: 」健將殺之，雄止之曰：「兒長成自當修改，何至便可如此！

translations.literal: Jian was about to kill him, but Xiong stopped him, saying: “When the boy grows he will reform himself—why go so far now!”
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian drew his sword, but Fu Xiong stayed his hand, arguing that age would tame the child.

sentences.zh: 」健乃止。

translations.literal: Jian then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian relented.

sentences.zh: 及長，力舉千鈞，雄勇好殺，手格猛獸，走及奔馬，擊刺騎射，冠絕一時。

translations.literal: When grown, his strength could lift a thousand jun; he was fierce, brave, and fond of killing; with his hands he grappled fierce beasts; running, he overtook galloping horses; in thrusting, riding, and shooting he had no peer of his age.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he could hoist weights beyond measure, delighted in slaughter, wrestled beasts bare-handed, outran horses, and excelled every rival in arms.

sentences.zh: 桓溫之來伐也，生單馬入陣，搴旗斬將者前後十數。

translations.literal: When Huan Wen came to attack, Sheng rode alone into the formation; the standards he seized and generals he beheaded numbered in the tens.
translations.idiomatic: Against Huan Wen’s invasion he charged solo into the ranks, snatching banners and beheading commanders time after time.

sentences.zh: 萇既死，健以讖言三羊五眼應符，故立為太子。

translations.literal: After Chang died, Jian, because a prophecy spoke of “three rams and five eyes” matching the Fu omen, therefore established him as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Fu Chang fell, Fu Jian chose him heir because omens spoke of three rams, five eyes, and the “Fu” sign.

sentences.zh: 健卒，僭即皇帝位，大赦境內，改年壽光，時也。

translations.literal: When Jian died, he usurped the imperial throne, granted a great amnesty within the realm, and changed the era name to Shouguang, as of that time.
translations.idiomatic: On Fu Jian’s death he seized the throne, declared a general amnesty, and adopted the reign title Shouguang.

sentences.zh: 尊其母強氏為皇太后，立妻梁氏為皇后。

translations.literal: He honored his mother Lady Qiang as empress dowager and established his wife Lady Liang as empress.
translations.idiomatic: He elevated Lady Qiang to empress dowager and Lady Liang to empress.

sentences.zh: 以呂婆樓為侍中、左大將軍，苻安領太尉，苻柳為征東大將軍、并州牧，鎮蒲阪，苻謏為鎮東大將軍、豫州牧，鎮陝城，自余封授有差。

translations.literal: He appointed Lü Lou as palace attendant and Left Grand General, Fu An as concurrent Grand Commandant, Fu Liu as General Who Conquers the East and Shepherd of Bing Province, garrisoning Puban, Fu Sou as General Who Garrisons the East and Shepherd of Yu Province, garrisoning Shancheng; the rest received graded enfeoffments and posts.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Lou became palace attendant and left grand general; Fu An took the grand commandant’s seal; Fu Liu held Bing as eastern conqueror from Puban; Fu Sou held Yu from Shancheng; others were ranked accordingly.

sentences.zh: 初，生將強懷與桓溫戰沒，其子延未及封而健死。

translations.literal: At first, when Sheng’s general Qiang Huai died fighting Huan Wen, his son Yan had not yet been enfeoffed when Jian died.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Huai, who had fallen battling Huan Wen, left a son Yan still without a title when Fu Jian died.

sentences.zh: 會生出遊，懷妻樊氏于道上書，論懷忠烈，請封其子。

translations.literal: It happened that Sheng went on an outing; Huai’s wife Lady Fan submitted a petition on the road, arguing Huai’s loyalty and valor and asking that her son be enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: While Fu Sheng was abroad, Lady Fan waylaid the cortège with a plea for her husband’s martyred honor and a fief for their son.

sentences.zh: 生怒，射而殺之。

translations.literal: Sheng grew angry, shot her with an arrow, and killed her.
translations.idiomatic: He answered with a bowshot and left her dead.

sentences.zh: 偽中書監胡文、中書令王魚言於生曰：「比頻有客星孛於大角，熒惑入于東井。

translations.literal: The false Palace Secretary Hu Wen and Palace Minister Wang Yu spoke to Sheng: “Recently a guest star has repeatedly cometed by Dajiao, and Mars has entered the Eastern Well.”
translations.idiomatic: Hu Wen and Wang Yu warned that a broom star haunted Dajiao and Mars sat in Dongjing—ill omens.

sentences.zh: 大角為帝坐，東井秦之分野，於占，不出三年，國有大喪，大臣戮死。

translations.literal: Dajiao is the emperor’s seat; the Eastern Well is the field division of Qin; in divination, within three years the state will suffer a great mourning and great ministers will be executed to death.
translations.idiomatic: Dajiao signified the throne; Dongjing mapped to Qin—astrologers foretold a royal death and slaughter of high ministers within three years.

sentences.zh: 願陛下遠追周文，修德以禳之，惠和群臣，以成康哉之美。

translations.literal: We hope Your Majesty will far emulate King Wen of Zhou, cultivate virtue to dispel it, be kind and harmonize the host of ministers, and complete the beauty of the Kang-era peace.”
translations.idiomatic: They begged him to imitate King Wen, mend his rule, and soothe the court to avert disaster.

sentences.zh: 」生曰：「皇后與朕對臨天下，亦足發塞大喪之變。

translations.literal: Sheng said: “The empress and I together face the All-under-Heaven—that is enough to block the change of a great mourning.”
translations.idiomatic: He replied that he and the empress ruled jointly, which ought to satisfy heaven’s demand for a great bereavement.

sentences.zh: 毛太傅、梁車騎、梁僕射受遺輔政，可謂大臣也。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Mao, General of Chariots Liang, and Vice Director Liang received the testamentary charge to assist government—they may be called great ministers.”
translations.idiomatic: The regents Mao, Liang the cavalry general, and Liang the vice director, he added, surely counted as the doomed ministers.

sentences.zh: 」於是殺其妻梁氏及太傅毛貴，車騎、尚書令梁楞，左僕射梁安。

translations.literal: Thereupon he killed his wife Lady Liang and Grand Tutor Mao Gui, General of Chariots and Minister Secretary Liang Leng, and Left Vice Director Liang An.
translations.idiomatic: He then murdered his empress, Grand Tutor Mao Gui, Minister Secretary Liang Leng, and Left Vice Director Liang An.

sentences.zh: 未凡，又誅侍中、丞相雷弱兒及其九子、二十七孫。

translations.literal: Before long, he also executed Palace Attendant and Chancellor Lei Ruo’er together with his nine sons and twenty-seven grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he extirpated Chancellor Lei Ruo’er’s entire close line—nine sons and twenty-seven grandsons.

sentences.zh: 諸羌悉叛。

translations.literal: All the Qiang rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Every Qiang clan rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 弱兒，南安羌酋也，剛鯁好直言，見生嬖臣趙韶、董榮亂政，每大言於朝，故榮等譖而誅之。

translations.literal: Ruo’er was chief of the Nan’an Qiang, stubborn and fond of blunt speech; seeing Sheng’s favorites Zhao Shao and Dong Rong disordering government, he often spoke loudly at court; therefore Rong and others slandered him and had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Ruo’er, a Nan’an Qiang chief who spoke his mind, had denounced the favorites Zhao Shao and Dong Rong; they framed him and brought about his death.

sentences.zh: 生雖在諒闇，游飲自若，荒耽淫虐，殺戮無道，常彎弓露刃以見朝臣，錘鉗鋸鑿備置左右。

translations.literal: Though Sheng was in the mourning shed, he roamed and drank as usual, wasteful, dissolute, cruel, and killing without the Way; he often appeared before court ministers with bared bow and blade; hammers, pincers, saws, and chisels were set ready to his left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Even in mourning he caroused, indulged every cruelty, and met officials with strung bow and naked steel while torturer’s tools waited at his elbow.

sentences.zh: 又納董榮之言，誅其司空王墮以應日蝕之災。

translations.literal: Further accepting Dong Rong’s words, he executed his Minister of Works Wang Duo to answer the disaster of a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Heeding Dong Rong, he sacrificed Minister of Works Wang Duo to “answer” an eclipse.

sentences.zh: 饗群臣於太極前殿，飲酣樂奏，生親歌以和之。

translations.literal: He feasted the host of ministers in the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate before the hall; when the drinking was deep and music played, Sheng himself sang to accompany it.
translations.idiomatic: He banqueted the bureaucracy in the forward hall of the Supreme Ultimate, conducting the chorus himself as cups circled.

sentences.zh: 命其尚書辛牢典勸，既而怒曰：「何不強酒？

translations.literal: He ordered his Minister Xin Lao to supervise the toasting; presently he angrily said: “Why do you not force the wine?”
translations.idiomatic: He put Xin Lao in charge of refills, then snarled why the guests were not forced to drink.

sentences.zh: 猶有坐者！

translations.literal: There are still men sitting sober!”
translations.idiomatic: Some still sat upright—sober.

sentences.zh: 」引弓射牢而殺之。

translations.literal: He drew his bow, shot Xin Lao, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He shot Xin Lao dead on the spot.

sentences.zh: 於是百僚大懼，無不引滿昏醉，汙服失冠，蓬頭僵僕，生以為樂。

translations.literal: Thereupon the hundred officials were greatly afraid; none failed to drain their cups to drunken stupor, soiling clothes, losing caps, hair disheveled, collapsed in heaps—Sheng took this as amusement.
translations.idiomatic: The court emptied every cup until men sprawled in vomit and lost headgear—Fu Sheng laughed at the spectacle.

sentences.zh: 生聞張祚見殺，玄靚幼沖，命其征東苻柳參軍閻負、梁殊使涼州，以書喻之。

translations.literal: When Sheng heard that Zhang Zuo had been killed and Xuanjing was young, he ordered his Eastern Conqueror Fu Liu’s staff advisers Yan Fu and Liang Shu to go to Liangzhou with a letter to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Zhang Zuo’s murder and Zhang Xuanjing’s minority, he dispatched Yan Fu and Liang Shu to Liangzhou under Fu Liu’s banner with a lecturing letter.

sentences.zh: 負、殊至姑臧，玄靚年幼，不見殊等。

translations.literal: When Fu and Shu reached Guzang, Xuanjing was young and did not receive Shu and the others.
translations.idiomatic: At Guzang the boy ruler declined to meet the envoys.

sentences.zh: 其涼州牧張瓘謂負、殊曰：「孤之本朝，世執忠節，遠宗大晉，臣無境外之交，君等何為而至？

translations.literal: The Governor of Liangzhou Zhang Guan said to Fu and Shu: “Our court has for generations held loyal integrity, reveres Great Jin at a distance, and your servant has no relations beyond the border—why have you come?”
translations.idiomatic: Regent Zhang Guan demanded why Qin envoys had come when Liangzhou owed allegiance only to Jin.

sentences.zh: 」負、殊曰：「晉王以鄰籓義好，有自來矣。

translations.literal: Fu and Shu said: “The Jin prince, out of neighborly goodwill, has had envoys come of themselves.”
translations.idiomatic: They answered that neighborly courtesy between courts was nothing new.

sentences.zh: 雖擁阻山河，然風通道會，不欲使羊、陸二公獨美於前。

translations.literal: Though mountains and rivers block the way, wind and roads still meet; he does not wish Yang and Lu alone to be praised in earlier times.”
translations.idiomatic: Mountains divide realms, yet messengers still pass; Qin would not leave the Yang–Lu rapprochement unmatched.

sentences.zh: 主上以欽明紹統，八表宅心，光被四海，格於天地。

translations.literal: The sovereign above, with enlightened succession, has the eight directions fix their hearts; his radiance covers the four seas and reaches to heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Their emperor, they said, ruled with clarity and won every quarter’s heart; his virtue filled the world.

sentences.zh: 晉王思與張王齊曜大明，交玉帛之好，兼與君公同金蘭之契，是以不遠而來，有何怪乎！

translations.literal: The Jin prince wishes together with the Zhang kings to share the bright sun, exchange silks as friendship, and with you, lord, swear a bond like metal and orchid—therefore he has come from afar; what is strange in that!”
translations.idiomatic: Qin sought friendship with the Zhangs as sworn allies—hence the long journey.

sentences.zh: 」瓘曰：「羊、陸一時之事，亦非純臣之義也。

translations.literal: Guan said: “The affair of Yang and Lu was a moment’s event, nor was it the pure minister’s righteousness.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guan dismissed the Yang–Lu parallel as opportunism, not steadfast loyalty.

sentences.zh: 本朝六世重光，固忠不貳，若與苻征東交玉帛之好者，便是上違先公純誠雅志，下乘河右遵奉之情。

translations.literal: Our court’s six generations have doubled the light, firmly loyal without twofold mind; if we were to exchange silks of friendship with Fu the Eastern Conqueror, that would be above betraying the former lords’ pure and sincere lofty intent, and below riding roughshod over the River-right’s duty of reverent submission.”
translations.idiomatic: Six generations of Liangzhou loyalty to Jin would be betrayed by treating with Fu Liu.

sentences.zh: 」負、殊曰：「昔微去殷，項伯歸漢，雖背君違親，前史美其先覺。

translations.literal: Fu and Shu said: “Anciently Wei left Yin, Xiang Bo went over to Han—though they turned from ruler and kin, earlier histories praised their foresight.”
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Liang cited lords who had wisely changed sides.

sentences.zh: 亡晉之餘，遠逃江會，天命去之，子故尊先王翻然改圖，北面二趙，蓋神算無方，鑒機而作。

translations.literal: The remnant of perished Jin fled far to the Jiang and Hui; Heaven’s mandate has left them; therefore your honored former kings turned their plans, faced north to the two Zhaos—surely divine calculation without fixed pattern, reading the moment and acting.”
translations.idiomatic: Jin was a spent force; past Liangzhou rulers had bowed to Zhao when heaven shifted—wise timing, they argued.

sentences.zh: 君公若欲稱制河西，眾旅非秦之敵，如欲宗歸遺晉，深乖先君雅旨，孰若遠蹤竇融附漢之規，近述先王歸趙之事，垂祚無窮，永享遐祉乎？

translations.literal: If you, lord, wish to style yourself over the River-west, your hosts cannot match Qin’s; if you wish to take Jin as your lineage, you deeply violate your late lords’ lofty intent—which is better than following afar Dou Rong’s precedent of attaching to Han, or narrating near your former kings’ submission to Zhao, extending fortune without end, forever enjoying distant blessing?”
translations.idiomatic: Independence was hopeless; clinging to Jin broke precedent; better follow Dou Rong and accept Qin’s suzerainty.

sentences.zh: 」瓘曰：「中州無信，好食誓言。

translations.literal: Guan said: “The Central Plain keeps no faith and loves to devour sworn oaths.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guan called the heartland treacherous oath-breakers.

sentences.zh: 往與石氏通好，旋見寇襲。

translations.literal: Formerly we communicated friendship with the Shi clan, then soon saw raid and attack.”
translations.idiomatic: Friendship with the Shi had ended in invasion.

sentences.zh: 中國之風，誡在昔日，不足復論通和之事也。

translations.literal: The custom of the Middle Kingdom—warning lies in former days—is not worth discussing further for matters of communication and peace.”
translations.idiomatic: Central Plains “good faith,” he said, was an old cautionary tale.

sentences.zh: 」負、殊曰：「三王異政，五帝殊風，趙多奸詐，秦以義信，豈可同年而語哉！

translations.literal: Fu and Shu said: “The three kings had different government, the five emperors different customs; Zhao was full of treachery and deceit, Qin by righteousness and good faith—how can they be spoken of in the same year!”
translations.idiomatic: Qin, they retorted, was nothing like the faithless Zhao.

sentences.zh: 張先、楊初皆擅兵一方，不供王貢，先帝命將擒之，宥其難恕之罪，加以爵封之榮。

translations.literal: Zhang Xian and Yang Chu each grasped arms in one region and did not supply royal tribute; the former emperor ordered generals to seize them, pardoned crimes hard to forgive, and added the glory of investiture.”
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Qin had spared and enfeoffed recalcitrant border lords such as Zhang Xian and Yang Chu.

sentences.zh: 今上道合二儀，慈弘山海，信符陰陽，禦物無際，不可以二趙相況也。

translations.literal: The present sovereign’s way joins the two poles, his kindness vast as mountain and sea, his trust matches yin and yang, and there is no limit to how he governs things—you cannot compare him to the two Zhaos.”
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng’s virtue, they claimed, outshone both Zhaos.

sentences.zh: 」瓘曰：「秦若兵強化盛，自可先取江南，天下自然盡為秦有，何辱征東之命！

translations.literal: Guan said: “If Qin’s arms are strong and its transformation flourishing, it can first take Jiangnan; then naturally the whole realm will belong to Qin—why demean yourself with an Eastern Conqueror’s command!”
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guan challenged them: if Qin were so mighty, conquer Jin first instead of jawboning Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 」負、殊曰：「先帝以大聖神武，開構鴻基，強燕納款，八州順軌。

translations.literal: Fu and Shu said: “The former emperor, with great sagely divine might, opened a grand foundation; mighty Yan tendered allegiance, eight provinces followed the track.”
translations.idiomatic: They praised the late emperor who had humbled Yan and won eight provinces.

sentences.zh: 主上欽明，道必隆世，慨徽號擁於河西，正朔未加吳會，以吳必須兵，涼可以義，故遣行人先申大好。

translations.literal: The sovereign above is reverently enlightened; his Way must uplift the age; he grieves that the honorific title is withheld west of the River while the correct calendar is not yet imposed on Wu and Kuai—because Wu must be taken by arms but Liangzhou can be won by righteousness, he therefore first sends envoys to declare great friendship.”
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng, they said, would use force on Wu but courtesy on Liangzhou—hence the embassy.

sentences.zh: 如君公不能蹈機而發者，正可緩江南數年之命，回師西旆，恐涼州弗可保也。

translations.literal: If you, lord, cannot tread the moment and rise in response, you may only prolong Jiangnan’s fate a few years; when he wheels the army west, I fear Liangzhou will not be secure.”
translations.idiomatic: Refusal would buy Jin a few years until Qin’s western march crushed Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 」瓘曰：「我跨據三州，帶甲十萬，西包昆域，東阻大河，伐人有餘，而況自固！

translations.literal: Guan said: “I stride over three provinces, armor on a hundred thousand, wrap the Kun regions in the west and block the great river in the east—I have surplus for attacking others, let alone defending myself!”
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guan boasted three provinces, a hundred thousand spears, and natural barriers.

sentences.zh: 秦何能為患！

translations.literal: What harm can Qin do!”
translations.idiomatic: What could Qin do to him?

sentences.zh: 」負、殊曰：「貴州險塞，孰若崤、函？

translations.literal: Fu and Shu said: “Your province’s perilous barriers—do they compare to Xiao and Han?”
translations.idiomatic: They asked whether Liangzhou’s defenses rivaled the Xiao–Han passes.

sentences.zh: 五郡之眾，何如秦、雍？

translations.literal: The hosts of five commanderies—how do they match Qin and Yong?”
translations.idiomatic: They compared five commanderies’ manpower to Qin and Yong.

sentences.zh: 張琚、杜洪因趙之成資，據天阻之固，策三秦之銳，藉陸海之饒，勁士風集，驍騎如雲，自謂天下可平，關中可固，先帝神矛一指，望旗冰解，人詠來蘇，不覺易主。

translations.literal: Zhang Ju and Du Hong, relying on Zhao’s accumulated resources, held fastnesses heaven made steep, wielded the keen edge of the three Qins, relied on the abundance of the land within the passes, crack troops gathered like wind, swift horse like clouds—they deemed the realm could be pacified and Guanzhong secured; one point of the former emperor’s divine spear, flags melted like ice, men sang of renewal, and without noticing they had changed masters.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ju and Du Hong had seemed invincible on Qin’s soil until Fu Jian’s spear shattered them overnight.

sentences.zh: 燕雖武視關東，猶以地勢之義，逆順之理，北面稱籓，貢不逾月。

translations.literal: Though Yan gazed martially east of the pass, still by the righteousness of terrain and the pattern of submission and resistance, it faced north as a vassal, tribute not exceeding a month.”
translations.idiomatic: Even mighty Yan had submitted within a month.

sentences.zh: 致肅慎楛矢，通九夷之珍；

translations.literal: They brought Sushen arrow-shafts and opened the treasures of the nine Yi;”
translations.idiomatic: Tribute flowed—Sushen arrows, goods of the nine Yi.

sentences.zh: 單于屈膝，名王內附。

translations.literal: the Chanyu knelt; famous kings attached within.”
translations.idiomatic: Chanyus knelt and tribal kings came in.

sentences.zh: 控弦之士百有餘萬，鼓行而濟西河者，君公何以抗之？

translations.literal: Drawn-bow warriors exceed a million; when they beat drums and march to cross the western River—how will you, lord, resist them?”
translations.idiomatic: Over a million bowmen could ford the west—how would Liangzhou stand?

sentences.zh: 盍追遵先王臣趙故事，世享大美，為秦之西籓。

translations.literal: Why not follow your former kings’ precedent of serving Zhao, forever enjoying great beauty, and be Qin’s western screen?”
translations.idiomatic: Better follow old kings who served Zhao and become Qin’s western bulwark.

sentences.zh: 」瓘曰：「然秦之德義加於天下，江南何以不賓？

translations.literal: Guan said: “Yet if Qin’s virtue and righteousness are laid on the whole realm, why does Jiangnan not submit?”
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guan asked why Jin still held out if Qin’s virtue was universal.

sentences.zh: 」負、殊曰：「文身之俗，負阻江山，道洿先叛，化盛後賓，自古而然，豈但今也！

translations.literal: Fu and Shu said: “The custom of tattooed bodies, relying on blocked rivers and mountains—when the Way is foul they rebel first; when transformation flourishes they submit afterward—thus it has been from antiquity; how only today!”
translations.idiomatic: They answered that southerners were tattooed barbarians behind rivers—rebellious when rule faltered, docile when culture triumphed.

sentences.zh: 故《詩》曰：'蠢爾蠻荊，大邦為仇。

translations.literal: Therefore the Classic of Poetry says: ‘You foolish Man and Jing tribes—the great state is your foe.’
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Odes: “Stupid Man and Jing—you make yourselves foes of the great state.”

sentences.zh: '言其不可以德義懷也。

translations.literal: ” It means they cannot be embraced with virtue and righteousness.”
translations.idiomatic: Meaning: they cannot be won by virtue alone.

sentences.zh: 」瓘曰：「秦據漢舊都，地兼將相，文武輔臣，領袖一時者誰也？

translations.literal: Guan said: “Qin occupies Han’s old capital, its territory combining general and minister—who are the civil and martial supporting ministers, leaders of the age?”
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guan asked who led Qin’s civil and martial elite.

sentences.zh: 」負、殊曰：「皇室懿籓，忠若公旦者，則大司馬、武都王安，征東大將軍、晉王柳；

translations.literal: Fu and Shu said: “Among the imperial house’s honored vassals, loyal as the Duke of Zhou, are the Grand Marshal, Prince of Wudu, Fu An, and the General Who Conquers the East, Prince of Jin, Fu Liu;”
translations.idiomatic: They began with princes Fu An and Fu Liu, paragons like the Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 文武兼才，神器秀拔，入可允厘百工，出能折沖萬里者，衛大將軍、廣平王黃眉，後將軍、清河王法，龍驤將軍、東海王堅之兄弟；

translations.literal: those who combine civil and martial talent, vessels of the divine regalia, outstanding in person—within they can harmonize the hundred crafts, without they can shatter enemy hosts at ten thousand li—are the younger brothers of the General of the Guards, Prince of Guangping, Fu Huangmei, the General of the Rear, Prince of Qinghe, Fu Fa, and the General of the Soaring Dragon, Prince of Donghai, Fu Jian;”
translations.idiomatic: Fu Huangmei, Fu Fa, and Fu Jian—brothers who could order the court or shatter armies.

sentences.zh: 其耆年碩德，德侔尚父者，則太師、錄尚書事、廣寧公魚遵；

translations.literal: those of hoary age and great virtue, whose virtue matches the Grand Duke Shang, are the Grand Tutor, Recorder of the Secretariat, Duke of Guangning, Yu Zun;”
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zun matched the Grand Duke of Shang in age and weight.

sentences.zh: 其清素剛嚴，骨鯁貞亮，則左光祿大夫強平，金紫光祿程肱、牛夷；

translations.literal: those pure, austere, rigid, and stern, upright in bone and bright in integrity, are the Left Counselor Guanglu Qiang Ping, and Jinzi Guanglu Cheng Gong and Niu Yi;”
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Ping, Cheng Gong, and Niu Yi embodied austere integrity.

sentences.zh: 博聞強識，探賾索幽，則中書監胡文，中書令王魚，黃門侍郎李柔；

translations.literal: those broad in hearing and strong in memory, who probe the hidden and search the subtle, are Palace Secretary Hu Wen, Palace Minister Wang Yu, and Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Li Rou;”
translations.idiomatic: Hu Wen, Wang Yu, and Li Rou were learned scholars.

sentences.zh: 雄毅厚重，權智無方，則左衛將軍李威，右衛將軍苻雅；

translations.literal: those fierce, steady, and weighty, with stratagem and wisdom without fixed pattern, are Left Guards General Li Wei and Right Guards General Fu Ya;”
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei and Fu Ya were steady strategists.

sentences.zh: 才識明達，令行禁止，則特進、領御史中丞梁平老，特進、光祿大夫強汪，侍中、尚書呂婆樓；

translations.literal: those bright in talent and judgment, whose orders go and prohibitions stop, are Special Companion, concurrent Censor-in-chief Liang Pinglao, Special Companion, Grand Master of Splendid Carriages Qiang Wang, Palace Attendant and Minister Lü Lou;”
translations.idiomatic: Liang Pinglao, Qiang Wang, and Lü Lou enforced crisp policy.

sentences.zh: 文史富贍，鬱為文宗，則尚書右僕射董榮，秘書監王颺，著作郎梁讜；

translations.literal: those rich in pattern and history, luxuriant as literary patriarchs, are Right Vice Director Dong Rong, Palace Library Director Wang Yang, and Editorial Director Liang Dan;”
translations.idiomatic: Dong Rong, Wang Yang, and Liang Dan headed letters.

sentences.zh: 驍勇多權略，攻必取，戰必勝，關、張之流，萬人之敵者，則前將軍、新興王飛，建切將軍鄧羌，立忠將軍彭越，安遠將軍范俱難，建武將軍徐盛；

translations.literal: those fierce and brave, rich in stratagem, who attack and always take, fight and always win—of the class of Guan and Zhang, enemies of ten thousand men—are Forward General, Prince of Xinxing, Fu Fei, General Who Establishes the Insignia Deng Qiang, General Who Upholds Loyalty Peng Yue, General Who Pacifies the Distance Fan Junan, General Who Establishes Martial Might Xu Sheng;”
translations.idiomatic: Fu Fei, Deng Qiang, Peng Yue, Fan Junan, and Xu Sheng matched Guan Yu and Zhang Fei in valor—Deng Qiang with the “establish insignia” general’s baton.

sentences.zh: 常伯納言，卿校牧守，則人皆文武，莫非才賢；

translations.literal: Among ordinary attendants who speak remonstrance, commanders and shepherds, the men are all civil and martial—none are not talented and worthy;”
translations.idiomatic: Every governor and colonel, they claimed, combined civil and martial gifts.

sentences.zh: 其餘懷經世之才，蘊佐時之略，守南山之操，遂而不奪者，王猛、硃肜之倫，相望于岩穀。

translations.literal: The rest who harbor talent to order the generation and store strategies to aid the times, who keep the temper of Mount South and pursue it without being turned—are men like Wang Meng and Zhu Rong, gazing at one another from cliff and valley.”
translations.idiomatic: Recluses such as Wang Meng and Zhu Rong still waited in the hills.

sentences.zh: 濟濟多士，焉可罄言！

translations.literal: A host of officers in such profusion—how can words exhaust it!”
translations.idiomatic: The roll call, they said, could run forever.

sentences.zh: 姚襄、張平一時之傑，各擁眾數萬，狼顧偏方，皆委忠獻款，請為臣妾。

translations.literal: Yao Xiang and Zhang Ping, heroes of the moment, each hold hosts of several tens of thousands, wolf-watch from a corner region, yet all have entrusted loyalty and offered sincerity, begging to be subjects and concubines.”
translations.idiomatic: Even Yao Xiang and Zhang Ping, warlords on the margins, had pledged fealty.

sentences.zh: 小不事大，《春秋》所誅，惟君公圖之。

translations.literal: To slight the great and serve the small is what the Spring and Autumn condemns—only you, lord, should plan it.”
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn censured those who scorned the great—only Zhang Guan could choose.

sentences.zh: 」瓘笑曰：「此事決之主上，非身所了。

translations.literal: Guan smiled and said: “This affair is decided by the sovereign above; it is not something my person can settle.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guan smiled that only the young prince could decide.

sentences.zh: 」負、殊曰：「涼王雖天縱英睿，然尚幼沖，君公居伊、霍之任，安危所系，見機之義，實在君公。

translations.literal: Fu and Shu said: “Though the Liang king is heaven-granted in heroic wisdom, he is still young; you, lord, hold the office of Yi and Huo—what security depends on is tied to you; the duty of reading the moment truly lies with you, lord.”
translations.idiomatic: They pressed him: the boy-king needed an Yi Yin or Huo Guang—Zhang Guan must act.

sentences.zh: 」瓘新輔政，河西所在兵起，懼秦師之至，乃言于玄靚，遣使稱籓，生因其所稱而授之。

translations.literal: Guan had newly taken up auxiliary government; troops rose everywhere along the River-west; he feared Qin’s army would arrive; therefore he spoke to Xuanjing, sent envoys to declare vassalage, and Sheng according to their declaration invested them.”
translations.idiomatic: With rebellion along the frontier and Qin looming, Zhang Guan persuaded Zhang Xuanjing to submit; Fu Sheng accepted the vassal’s titles.

sentences.zh: 慕容俊遣將慕輿長卿等率眾七千入自軹關，攻幽州刺史張哲于裴氏堡。

translations.literal: Murong Jun sent general Moyu Changqing and others leading a host of seven thousand in through Zhi Pass, attacking Inspector of You Province Zhang Zhe at Peishi Fort.”
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun dispatched Moyu Changqing with seven thousand men through Zhi Pass against Zhang Zhe at Peishi Fort.

sentences.zh: 晉將軍劉度等率眾四千，攻青州刺史袁朗于盧氏。

translations.literal: Jin general Liu Du and others led a host of four thousand, attacking Inspector of Qing Province Yuan Lang at Lushi.”
translations.idiomatic: Jin’s Liu Du struck Yuan Lang at Lushi with four thousand men.

sentences.zh: 生遣其前將軍苻飛距晉，建節鄧羌距燕。

translations.literal: Sheng sent his Forward General Fu Fei to oppose Jin, and General Who Establishes the Insignia Deng Qiang to oppose Yan.”
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng ordered Fu Fei against Jin and Deng Qiang against Yan.

sentences.zh: 飛未至而度退。

translations.literal: Before Fei arrived, Du withdrew.”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Du retreated before Fu Fei arrived.

sentences.zh: 羌及長卿戰于堡南，大敗之，獲長卿及甲首二千七百餘級。

translations.literal: Qiang and Changqing fought south of the fort; he greatly defeated them, captured Changqing, and took more than 2,700 armored heads.”
translations.idiomatic: Deng Qiang crushed Moyu Changqing below the fort, taking him prisoner and over 2,700 heads.

sentences.zh: 姚襄率眾萬餘，攻其平陽太守苻產于匈奴堡，苻柳救之，為襄所敗，引還蒲阪。

translations.literal: Yao Xiang led a host of more than ten thousand, attacking his Governor of Pingyang Fu Chan at the Xiongnu Fort; Fu Liu rescued him, was defeated by Xiang, and led the army back to Puban.”
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang besieged Fu Chan at the Xiongnu Fort; Fu Liu’s relief column failed and limped back to Puban.

sentences.zh: 襄遂攻堡，克之，殺苻產，盡坑其眾，遣使從生假道，將還隴西。

translations.literal: Xiang thereupon attacked the fort, took it, killed Fu Chan, buried his entire force alive in pits, sent envoys to Sheng begging right of way, intending to return to Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang stormed the fort, executed Fu Chan, massacred the garrison, then asked Fu Sheng for safe passage west to Longxi.

sentences.zh: 生將許之，苻堅諫曰：「姚襄，人傑也，今還隴西，必為深害，不如誘以厚利，伺隙而擊之。

translations.literal: Sheng was about to agree; Fu Jian remonstrated: “Yao Xiang is an outstanding man; if he returns to Longxi he will surely become a deep harm—better lure him with rich gifts and strike when a gap appears.”
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng meant to grant passage; Fu Jian urged him to bait Yao Xiang instead and destroy him before he reached Longxi.

sentences.zh: 」生乃止。

translations.literal: Sheng then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 遣使拜襄官爵，襄不受，斬其使者，焚所送章策，寇掠河東。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to invest Xiang with office and rank; Xiang refused, beheaded the envoys, burned the seals and patents they had brought, and raided Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys bearing titles were slain; Yao Xiang scorched the credentials and ravaged Hedong.

sentences.zh: 生怒，命其大將軍張平討之。

translations.literal: Sheng grew angry and ordered his Grand General Zhang Ping to chastise him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng tasked Grand General Zhang Ping with crushing him.

sentences.zh: 襄乃卑辭厚幣與平結為兄弟，平更與襄通和。

translations.literal: Xiang then used humble language and rich bribes to bond with Ping as sworn brothers, and Ping instead communicated peace with Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang bought Zhang Ping with gifts and flattery; the general switched sides.

sentences.zh: 生髮三輔人營渭橋，金紫光祿大夫程肱以妨農害時，上疏極諫。

translations.literal: Sheng mobilized men of the Three Adjuncts to build works at the Wei bridge; Grand Master of Golden Splendor and Purple Radiance Cheng Gong, because it harmed farming and the seasons, submitted a memorial of stern remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng drafted the Three Adjuncts to labor on a Wei River bridge; Cheng Gong protested that the corvée ruined the harvest.

sentences.zh: 生怒，殺之。

translations.literal: Sheng grew angry and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng had him executed.

sentences.zh: 長安大風，髮屋拔樹，行人顛頓，宮中奔擾，或稱賊至，宮門晝閉，五日乃止。

translations.literal: Great wind struck Chang’an—tearing off roofs, uprooting trees, throwing travelers down; inside the palace there was panic flight; some cried that bandits had come; palace gates closed by day; five days before it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: A gale ripped Chang’an apart; courtiers screamed of raiders and sealed the gates for five days.

sentences.zh: 生推告賊者，殺之，刳而出其心。

translations.literal: Sheng investigated those who had reported bandits, killed them, and gouged out their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He blamed the rumor-mongers, cut out their hearts, and left them dead.

sentences.zh: 左光祿大夫強平諫曰：「元正盛旦，日有蝕之，正陽神朔，昏風大起，兼水旱不時，獸災未息，此皆由陛下不勉強于政事，乖和氣所致也。

translations.literal: Left Counselor Guanglu Qiang Ping remonstrated: “On the great dawn of the New Year the sun was eclipsed; on the first sacred day of the month a great dark wind arose; moreover flood and drought do not come in season, and the scourge of beasts has not ceased—all this is because Your Majesty does not exert yourself in government, and harmony is thrown awry.”
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Ping cited eclipse, ill winds, drought, and man-eating beasts as heaven’s rebuke of Fu Sheng’s neglect.

sentences.zh: 願陛下務養元元，平章百姓，棄纖介之嫌，含山嶽之過，致敬宗社，愛禮公卿，去秋霜之威，垂三春之澤，則奸回寢止，妖昆自消，乾靈祗祐皇家，永保無窮之美矣。

translations.literal: “I hope Your Majesty will surely nurture the common folk, give peace to the hundred surnames, cast aside hair’s-breadth grudges, embrace mountain-like faults, show reverence to the ancestral altars, cherish ritual toward the dukes and ministers, put away autumn-frost severity, and let fall springlike grace—then treacherous ways will lie still, uncanny omens will vanish of themselves, High Heaven will bless the house, and endless beauty will be preserved forever.”
translations.idiomatic: He begged for mercy, reform, and reconciliation so omens would fade.

sentences.zh: 」生怒，以為妖言，鑿其頂而殺之。

translations.literal: Sheng grew angry, deemed it sorcerous talk, bored his skull open, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng called it witchcraft, trepanned his skull, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 平之囚也，偽衛將軍苻黃眉、前將軍苻飛、建節鄧羌侍宴禁中，叩頭固諫，以太后為言。

translations.literal: When Ping was imprisoned, Guard General Fu Huangmei, Forward General Fu Fei, and Deng Qiang who Establishes the Insignia attended a feast within the forbidden precincts, knocked their heads in firm remonstrance, and spoke invoking the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: While Qiang Ping languished in prison, Fu Huangmei, Fu Fei, and Deng Qiang banqueted inside the palace and begged clemency in the dowager’s name.

sentences.zh: 平即生母強氏之弟也。

translations.literal: Ping was the younger brother of Sheng’s mother Lady Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Ping was Empress Dowager Qiang’s brother.

sentences.zh: 生既弗許，強氏憂恨而死。

translations.literal: Since Sheng would not grant it, Lady Qiang died of worry and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng refused; the dowager died of grief.

sentences.zh: 生下書曰：「朕受皇天之命，承祖宗之業，君臨萬邦，子育百姓，嗣統已來，有何不善，而謗讟之音扇滿天下。

translations.literal: Sheng issued an edict: “We have received the charge of August Heaven, inherited the enterprise of the ancestors, lord it over myriad regions, and cherish the hundred surnames as children—since We succeeded the line, what have We done wrong, that slanderous voices fan and fill the realm?”
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng published a rant: he had heaven’s mandate—why did the world slander him?

sentences.zh: 殺不過千，而謂刑虐。

translations.literal: “The killed do not pass a thousand, yet they call Our punishments cruel.”
translations.idiomatic: “Fewer than a thousand dead, yet they call me cruel.”

sentences.zh: 行者比肩，未足為稀。

translations.literal: “Men walking shoulder to shoulder is not enough to count as rare.”
translations.idiomatic: “Corpses lining the roads are nothing special.”

sentences.zh: 方當峻刑極罰，復如朕何！

translations.literal: “We are about to sharpen punishments to the utmost—what can they do to Us!”
translations.idiomatic: “Wait until I tighten the noose—then see what they say!”

sentences.zh: 」時猛獸及狼大暴，晝則斷道，夜則髮屋，惟害人而不食六畜。

translations.literal: ” At that time fierce beasts and wolves ran riot; by day they cut the roads, by night they tore roofs; they harmed only people and did not eat the six domestic animals.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile wolves and brutes blocked daylight travel, tore roofs at night, and killed humans but left livestock alone.

sentences.zh: 自生立一年，獸殺七百餘人，百姓苦之，皆聚而邑居。

translations.literal: From the year Sheng was established, beasts killed more than seven hundred people; the people suffered, all gathering to live in walled settlements.
translations.idiomatic: In his first year beasts slew over seven hundred; peasants fled into fortified hamlets.

sentences.zh: 為害滋甚，遂廢農桑，內外兇懼。

translations.literal: The harm grew worse; farming and sericulture were abandoned; inside and outside all were frightened.
translations.idiomatic: Fields went untilled; terror gripped city and countryside.

sentences.zh: 群臣奏請禳災，生曰：「野獸饑則食人，飽當自止，終不能累年為患也。

translations.literal: The host of ministers memorialized asking to perform rites to dispel disaster; Sheng said: “When wild beasts hunger they eat men; when sated they will stop of themselves—they cannot plague us for years on end.”
translations.idiomatic: Ministers sought exorcisms; Fu Sheng sneered that hungry beasts simply needed feeding.

sentences.zh: 天豈不子愛群生，而年年降罰，正以百姓犯罪不已，將助朕專殺而施刑教故耳。

translations.literal: “Does not Heaven cherish the myriad lives? Yet year after year it sends punishment—precisely because the common people do not cease committing crimes, intending to help Us specialize in killing and apply punitive instruction.”
translations.idiomatic: He claimed heaven egged him on to slaughter sinners.

sentences.zh: 但勿犯罪，何為怨天而尤人哉！」

translations.literal: “Only do not commit crimes—why rail at Heaven and blame others!”
translations.idiomatic: “Stop sinning—then quit blaming heaven!”

sentences.zh: 生如阿房，遇兄與妹俱行者，逼令為非禮，不從，生怒殺之。

translations.literal: Sheng went to Epang, met a brother and sister walking together, forced them to commit incest; they refused—Sheng killed them in anger.
translations.idiomatic: At Epang he forced a brother and sister into incest and murdered them when they refused.

sentences.zh: 又宴群臣於咸陽故城，有後至者，皆斬之。

translations.literal: He also feasted the host of ministers at the old city of Xianyang; any who arrived late were all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: At an old Xianyang banquet he beheaded every latecomer.

sentences.zh: 嘗使太醫令程延合安胎藥，問人參好惡並藥分多少，延曰：「雖小小不具，自可堪用。

translations.literal: Once he had Imperial Physician-in-Chief Cheng Yan compound a fetus-quieting drug and asked how good the ginseng was and the proportions of ingredients; Yan said: “Though it is slightly incomplete in small ways, it can still serve.”
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Cheng Yan to brew a pregnancy draft; asked about the ginseng, Yan said the mix was slightly short yet usable.

sentences.zh: 」生以為譏其目，鑿延目出，然後斬之。

translations.literal: Sheng thought he mocked Our eye, bored out Yan’s eyes, then beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng decided “incomplete” mocked his blind eye, gouged Cheng Yan’s eyes, then took his head.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「太白犯東井。

translations.literal: The responsible office reported: “Venus encroaches on the Eastern Well.”
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported Venus trespassing Dongjing.

sentences.zh: 東井，秦之分也，太白罰星，必有暴兵起于京師。

translations.literal: “The Eastern Well is Qin’s field division; Venus is the punishing star—there is sure to be sudden arms rising from the capital.”
translations.idiomatic: They warned that Dongjing mapped to Qin and Venus meant mutiny in the capital.

sentences.zh: 」生曰：「星入井者，必將渴耳，何所怪乎！」

translations.literal: ” Sheng said: “When a star enters a well, it must be thirsty—what is strange in that!”
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng retorted that stars in a well only meant they were thirsty.

sentences.zh: 姚襄遣姚蘭、王欽盧待招動鄜城、定陽、北地、芹川諸羌胡，皆應之，有眾二萬七千，進據黃落。

translations.literal: Yao Xiang sent Yao Lan and Wang Qinlu to summon and stir the Qiang and Hu of Fucheng, Dingyang, Beidi, and Qinchuan; all responded; he had a host of twenty-seven thousand and advanced to occupy Huangluo.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Lan and Wang Qinlu rallied Qiang and Hu bands at Fucheng, Dingyang, Beidi, and Qinchuan—twenty-seven thousand strong—and seized Huangluo.

sentences.zh: 生遣苻黃眉、苻堅、鄧羌率步騎萬五千討之。

translations.literal: Sheng sent Fu Huangmei, Fu Jian, and Deng Qiang leading fifteen thousand foot and horse to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng dispatched Fu Huangmei, Fu Jian, and Deng Qiang with fifteen thousand men.

sentences.zh: 襄深溝高壘，固守不戰。

translations.literal: Xiang dug deep moats and raised high ramparts, firmly defending and not fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang went behind walls and refused battle.

sentences.zh: 鄧羌說黃眉曰：「傷弓之鳥，落於虛發。

translations.literal: Deng Qiang urged Huangmei: “A bird wounded by the bow falls to an empty release.”
translations.idiomatic: Deng Qiang said a spooked bird drops to a blank shot.

sentences.zh: 襄頻為桓溫、張平所敗，銳氣喪矣。

translations.literal: Xiang has repeatedly been defeated by Huan Wen and Zhang Ping; his keen edge is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen and Zhang Ping had already broken his spirit.

sentences.zh: 今謀固壘不戰，是窮寇也。

translations.literal: Now that he plots to hold his fort and not fight, he is a cornered bandit.
translations.idiomatic: Hiding behind earthworks, he was a trapped foe.

sentences.zh: 襄性剛很，易以剛動，若長驅鼓行，直壓其壘，襄必忿而出師，可一戰擒也。

translations.literal: Xiang’s nature is stubborn and harsh; he is easily moved by hardness—if we beat drums on a long drive and press straight on his fort, Xiang is sure to rage and come out; we can capture him in one battle.”
translations.idiomatic: Provoke the stubborn chief with a frontal rush and he would storm out to be crushed.

sentences.zh: 」黃眉從之，遣羌率騎三千軍於壘門。

translations.literal: Huangmei followed this, sent Qiang leading three thousand horse to encamp at the fort gate.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Huangmei agreed; Deng Qiang planted three thousand riders at the gate.

sentences.zh: 襄怒，盡銳出戰。

translations.literal: Xiang grew angry and came out with his full keen edge to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang hurled his best troops into the open.

sentences.zh: 羌偽不勝，引騎而退，襄追之于三原，羌回騎距襄。

translations.literal: Qiang feigned defeat, led his horse in retreat; Xiang pursued him to Sanyuan; Qiang wheeled his horse to oppose Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Qiang feigned flight, drew Yao Xiang to Sanyuan, then wheeled to fight.

sentences.zh: 俄而黃眉與堅至，大戰，斬之，盡俘其眾，黃眉等振旅而歸。

translations.literal: Presently Huangmei and Jian arrived; they fought a great battle, beheaded him, captured his entire host; Huangmei and the others returned with drums of victory.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Huangmei and Fu Jian arrived, slew Yao Xiang, bagged his army, and marched home in triumph.

sentences.zh: 黃眉雖有大功，生不加旌賞，每於眾中辱之。

translations.literal: Though Huangmei had great merit, Sheng added no banner reward and often humiliated him before the host.
translations.idiomatic: Despite the victory, Fu Sheng never honored Fu Huangmei and routinely shamed him before the troops.

sentences.zh: 黃眉怒，謀殺生自立，事發，伏誅，其王公親戚多有死者。

translations.literal: Huangmei grew angry, plotted to kill Sheng and set himself up; the affair leaked; he was executed by strangulation; many of the princes, dukes, and kin died.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Huangmei plotted a coup, failed, died, and dragged many kinsmen to execution.

sentences.zh: 初，生夢大魚食蒲，又長安謠曰：「東海大魚化為龍，男便為王女為公。

translations.literal: At first Sheng dreamed a great fish ate cattail; moreover a Chang’an rhyme ran: “The great fish of the Eastern Sea turns into a dragon; the men become kings, the women dukes.”
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed a fish devouring reeds; a ditty spoke of a sea fish becoming a dragon.
