sentences.zh: 問在何所洛門東。

translations.literal: “Ask where they are—east of the Luo Gate.”
translations.idiomatic: “Look east of Luomen—that is their seat.”

sentences.zh: 」東海，苻堅封也，時為龍驤將軍，第在洛門之東。

translations.literal: ” The Eastern Sea was Fu Jian’s fief; at the time he was General of the Soaring Dragon, and his mansion lay east of the Luo Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The riddle pointed at Fu Jian, Soaring Dragon general, whose manor stood east of Luomen.

sentences.zh: 生不知是堅，以謠夢之故，誅其侍中、太師、錄尚書事魚遵及其七子、十孫。

translations.literal: Sheng did not realize it was Jian; because of the rhyme and dream he executed his Palace Attendant, Grand Tutor, and Recorder of the Secretariat Yu Zun together with his seven sons and ten grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Misreading the omen, Fu Sheng slaughtered Grand Tutor Yu Zun’s whole close line.

sentences.zh: 時又謠曰：「百里望空城，鬱鬱何青青。

translations.literal: At that time another rhyme ran: “For a hundred li one gazes on empty cities, how lushly green.”
translations.idiomatic: Another song spoke of green, empty cities stretching a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 瞎兒不知法，仰不見天星。

translations.literal: “The blind boy knows no law; looking up he cannot see the stars of heaven.”
translations.idiomatic: It mocked the one-eyed king who could not read heaven’s signs.

sentences.zh: 」於是悉壞諸空城以禳之。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he utterly demolished the various empty cities to dispel it.
translations.idiomatic: He razed empty towns to break the spell.

sentences.zh: 金紫光祿大夫牛夷懼不免禍，請出鎮上洛。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Golden Splendor and Purple Radiance Niu Yi, fearing he could not escape disaster, asked to go out and garrison Shangluo.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Yi begged for a frontier post to escape the purge.

sentences.zh: 生曰：「卿忠肅篤敬，宜左右朕躬，豈有外鎮之理。

translations.literal: Sheng said: “You are loyal, solemn, and devoted—fit to attend Our person at left and right; how could there be reason for an outer garrison?”
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng replied that such a loyal man must stay at court.

sentences.zh: 」改授中軍。

translations.literal: ” He changed the appointment to Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: He reassigned him to the central army instead.

sentences.zh: 夷懼，歸而自殺。

translations.literal: Yi feared this, returned home, and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Yi went home and committed suicide.

sentences.zh: 初，生少凶暴嗜酒，健臨死，恐其不能保全家業，誡之曰：「酋師、大臣若不從汝命，可漸除之。

translations.literal: At first Sheng in youth was violent and fond of wine; when Jian was dying he feared Sheng could not preserve the family enterprise and admonished him: “If tribal chiefs and great ministers do not obey your commands, you may gradually remove them.”
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian on his deathbed warned the drunken, brutal youth to prune any chief or minister who defied him.

sentences.zh: 」及即偽位，殘虐滋甚，耽湎於酒，無復晝夜。

translations.literal: ” When he assumed the usurped throne, cruelty and slaughter grew worse; he drowned in wine, no longer distinguishing day from night.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned, he drank without night or day and killed more savagely than ever.

sentences.zh: 群臣朔望朝謁，罕有見者，或至暮方出，臨朝輒怒，惟行殺戮。

translations.literal: The host of ministers on the new and full moon audiences rarely saw him; sometimes he emerged only toward dusk; whenever he faced court he was angry and only carried out killing.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers seldom saw him before dusk; every audience ended in executions.

sentences.zh: 動連月昏醉，文奏因之遂寢。

translations.literal: For whole months he moved in drunken stupor; memorials on that account went to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Month-long binges left state papers unanswered.

sentences.zh: 納奸佞之言，賞罰失中。

translations.literal: He accepted slanderous flatterers’ words; rewards and punishments missed the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Flatterers set policy; justice vanished.

sentences.zh: 左右或言陛下聖明宰世，天下惟歌太平。

translations.literal: Those at his side who said Your Majesty sagely illumines the age and the realm alone sings of great peace—
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers who praised his sage rule—

sentences.zh: 生曰：「媚於我也。

translations.literal: Sheng said: “You flatter Us.”
translations.idiomatic: he branded flattery.

sentences.zh: 」引而斬之。

translations.literal: ” He led them forth and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: He had them led out and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 或言陛下刑罰微過。

translations.literal: Some said Your Majesty’s punishments are slightly excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Others hinted his punishments were harsh—

sentences.zh: 曰：「汝謗我也。

translations.literal: He said: “You slander Us.”
translations.idiomatic: he called it slander.

sentences.zh: 」亦斬之。

translations.literal: ” He beheaded them as well.
translations.idiomatic: They too lost their heads.

sentences.zh: 所幸妻妾小有忤旨，便殺之，流其屍于渭水。

translations.literal: The concubines he favored, if they slightly disobeyed his intent, he killed them and floated their corpses on the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Favored women who crossed him were killed and dumped in the Wei.

sentences.zh: 又遣宮人與男子裸交於殿前。

translations.literal: He also sent palace women to couple naked with men before the hall.
translations.idiomatic: He staged public orgies in the throne hall.

sentences.zh: 生剝牛羊驢馬，活爓雞豚鵝，三五十為群，放之殿中。

translations.literal: He flayed cattle, sheep, donkeys, and horses, and scorched chickens, pigs, and geese alive, thirty or fifty at a time, releasing them inside the hall.
translations.idiomatic: He tore the hides from livestock and roasted poultry alive in batches inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 或剝死囚面皮，令其歌舞，引群臣觀之，以為嬉樂。

translations.literal: Sometimes he flayed condemned men’s faces and made them sing and dance, leading the host of ministers to watch, taking it as sport.
translations.idiomatic: He skinned convicts’ faces, forced them to perform, and made officials watch for sport.

sentences.zh: 宗室、勳舊、親戚、忠良殺害略盡，王公在位者悉以疾告歸，人情危駭，道路以目。

translations.literal: Imperial kin, merit old-timers, in-laws, and the loyal and good were killed nearly to extinction; princes and dukes in office all pleaded illness and retired; human hearts were terrified; on the road people signaled only with their eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Clan, veterans, and loyalists perished; nobles feigned illness; folk dared only exchange glances on the street.

sentences.zh: 既自有目疾，其所諱者不足、不具、少、無、缺、傷、殘、毀、偏、只之言皆不得道，左右忤旨而死者不可勝紀，至於截脛、刳胎、拉脅、鋸頸者動有千數。

translations.literal: Since he himself had an eye ailment, he tabooed the words insufficient, incomplete, few, none, lacking, injured, crippled, ruined, lopsided, only—none might be spoken; those at his side who offended his intent and died could not be counted; as for cutting shins, gouging wombs, breaking ribs, sawing necks—these ran to thousands at a move.
translations.idiomatic: His blind eye made words like “lacking” or “one-eyed” lethal; mutilations—shin-cutting, womb-gouging—numbered in the thousands.

sentences.zh: 太史令康權言於生曰：「昨夜三月並出，勃星入於太微，遂入于東井。

translations.literal: Astrologer-in-Chief Kang Quan spoke to Sheng: “Last night three moons appeared together; a comet entered the Supreme Tenuity, then entered the Eastern Well.”
translations.idiomatic: Kang Quan reported three moons and a comet in Taiwei and Dongjing.

sentences.zh: 兼自去月上旬沈陰不雨，迄至於今，將有下人謀上之禍，深願陛下修德以消之。

translations.literal: “Moreover from the first decade of last month it has been sunken and overcast without rain down to now—there will be disaster of inferiors plotting against superiors; I deeply hope Your Majesty will cultivate virtue to dispel it.”
translations.idiomatic: Weeks without sun foretold regicide, he said—unless the king reformed.

sentences.zh: 」生怒，以為妖言，撲而殺之。

translations.literal: ” Sheng grew angry, deemed it sorcerous talk, beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng beat Kang Quan to death for “witch talk.”

sentences.zh: 生夜對侍婢曰：「阿法兄弟亦不可信，明當除之。

translations.literal: Sheng said by night to an attending maid: “The Fa brothers too are not to be trusted; tomorrow We shall eliminate them.”
translations.idiomatic: He told a maid he would kill Fu Fa’s faction next dawn.

sentences.zh: 」是夜清河王苻法夢神告之曰：「旦將禍集汝門，惟先覺者可以免之。

translations.literal: ” That night Prince of Qinghe Fu Fa dreamed a god told him: “At dawn disaster will gather at your gate—only the forewarned may escape.”
translations.idiomatic: That night Fu Fa dreamed a god warning of dawn attack.

sentences.zh: 」寤而心悸。

translations.literal: ” Awakening, his heart pounded.
translations.idiomatic: He woke in terror.

sentences.zh: 會侍婢來告，乃與特進梁平老、強汪等率壯士數百人潛入雲龍門，苻堅與呂婆樓率麾下三百餘人鼓噪繼進，宿衛將士皆舍杖歸堅。

translations.literal: When the attending maid came to report, he then with Special Companion Liang Pinglao, Qiang Wang, and others led several hundred stalwarts to slip into the Cloud Dragon Gate; Fu Jian and Lü Lou led more than three hundred of their command shouting and pressing forward; the night-watch generals and soldiers all cast aside staves and submitted to Jian.
translations.idiomatic: The maid warned Fu Fa; with Liang Pinglao and Qiang Wang he seized the Cloud Dragon Gate as Fu Jian and Lü Lou stormed in—guards threw down their weapons for Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 生猶昏寐未寤。

translations.literal: Sheng was still in drunken sleep and had not awakened.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Sheng lay drunk and unaware.

sentences.zh: 堅眾既至，引生置於別室，廢之為越王，俄而殺之。

translations.literal: When Jian’s host had arrived, they led Sheng forth and placed him in a separate chamber, deposed him as Prince of Yue, and before long killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian’s men dragged him out, demoted him to Prince of Yue, then killed him.

sentences.zh: 生臨死猶飲酒數斗，昏醉無所知矣。

translations.literal: Sheng at the point of death still drank several dou of wine, insensibly drunk and knowing nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He drank himself insensible even at the end.

sentences.zh: 時年二十三，在位二年，偽諡厲王。

translations.literal: He was twenty-three years old, had reigned two years, and received the false posthumous title Prince Li.
translations.idiomatic: He died at twenty-three after two years on the throne, posthumously styled the cruel Prince Li.

sentences.zh: 洪季子 雄

translations.literal: Hong’s youngest son: Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xiong—Fu Hong’s youngest son.

translations.literal: A horizontal rule in the original table layout.
translations.idiomatic: Another typographic rule follows.

sentences.zh: 苻雄，字元才，洪之季子也。

translations.literal: Fu Xiong, courtesy name Yuancai, was Hong’s youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xiong, style Yuancai, was the last son of Fu Hong.

sentences.zh: 少善兵書，而多謀略，好施下士，便弓馬，有政術。

translations.literal: In youth he was good at military texts, full of stratagems, fond of generosity and condescending to men of talent, handy with bow and horse, and possessed of methods of government.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered military classics, schemed generously, won soldiers’ hearts, rode and shot well, and governed shrewdly.

sentences.zh: 健僭位，為佐命元勳，權侔人主，而謙恭奉法。

translations.literal: When Jian usurped the throne, he was a founding pillar of merit; his power matched the ruler’s, yet he was humble and observed the law.
translations.idiomatic: Under Fu Jian’s usurpation he was pillar of the state—mightier than most kings yet modest and lawful.

sentences.zh: 健常曰：「元才，吾姬旦也。

translations.literal: Jian often said: “Yuancai is Our Ji Dan.”
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian called him his own Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 」及卒，健哭之歐血，曰：「天不欲吾定四海邪？

translations.literal: ” When he died, Jian wept until he vomited blood, saying: “Does Heaven not wish Us to settle the four seas?”
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Xiong died, Fu Jian wept blood and asked if heaven blocked his conquests.

sentences.zh: 何奪元才之速也！

translations.literal: “Why snatch Yuancai away so fast!”
translations.idiomatic: “Why take Yuancai so soon!”

sentences.zh: 」子堅，別有載記。

translations.literal: ” His son Jian has a separate record.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu Jian has his own annals.

sentences.zh: 王墮

translations.literal: Wang Duo
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duo

sentences.zh: 王墮，字安生，京兆霸城人也。

translations.literal: Wang Duo, courtesy name Ansheng, was a man of Bashicheng in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duo, style Ansheng, came from Bashicheng in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 博學有雄才，明天文圖緯。

translations.literal: He was broadly learned and had heroic talent, understood astronomy, charts, and weft-text prophecies.
translations.idiomatic: He was a polymath, astrologer, and prognosticator.

sentences.zh: 苻洪征梁犢，以墮為司馬，謂洪曰：「讖言苻氏應王，公其人也。

translations.literal: When Fu Hong campaigned against Liang Du, he made Duo his chief of staff; Duo said to Hong: “The prophecy says the Fu house shall rule—you are that man.”
translations.idiomatic: As Fu Hong’s chief of staff against Liang Du, Wang Duo declared the “Fu shall reign” omen pointed at Hong.

sentences.zh: 」洪深然之。

translations.literal: Hong deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hong believed him utterly.

sentences.zh: 及為宰相，著匪躬之稱。

translations.literal: When he became chancellor, he earned the reputation of denying self for duty.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister he was known for tireless, selfless service.

sentences.zh: 健常歎曰：「天下群官皆如王令君者，陰陽曷不和乎！

translations.literal: Jian often sighed: “If every official in the realm were like Director Wang, how could yin and yang fail to harmonize!”
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian used to sigh that if every magistrate matched Director Wang, heaven and earth would stay in tune.

sentences.zh: 」甚敬重之。

translations.literal: ” He greatly revered and honored him.
translations.idiomatic: He held Wang Duo in the highest regard.

sentences.zh: 性剛峻疾惡，雅好直言。

translations.literal: By nature he was rigid and stern, hating evil, and by inclination loved blunt speech.
translations.idiomatic: Rigid, upright, and outspoken, he despised corruption.

sentences.zh: 疾董榮、強國如仇讎，每於朝見之際，略不與言。

translations.literal: He hated Dong Rong and Qiang Guo as mortal foes; whenever they met at court he would not speak to them at all.
translations.idiomatic: He loathed Dong Rong and his fellow favorite Zhao Shao—ministers who had wormed into power—and cut them dead at every audience.

sentences.zh: 人謂之曰：「董尚書貴幸一時，公宜降意。

translations.literal: Someone said to him: “Director Dong is honored and favored for the moment—you ought to bend your will.”
translations.idiomatic: Advisers warned him to humor the all-powerful Director Dong.

sentences.zh: 」墮曰：「董龍是何雞狗，而令國士與之言乎！

translations.literal: ” Duo said: “What sort of chicken or dog is Dong Long, that a man of the state should speak with him!”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duo retorted, “Dong Long is a cur—why should a gentleman of the realm address him?”

sentences.zh: 」榮聞而慚恨，遂勸生誅之。

translations.literal: ” When Rong heard this he was ashamed and resentful, and thereupon urged Sheng to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Rong, humiliated, talked Fu Sheng into killing him.

sentences.zh: 及刑，榮謂墮曰：「君今復敢數董龍作雞狗？

translations.literal: When it came to execution, Rong said to Duo: “Do you still dare to count Dong Long as chicken or dog?”
translations.idiomatic: At the scaffold Dong Rong sneered, “Still calling Dong Long a dog?”

sentences.zh: 」墮瞋目而叱之。

translations.literal: ” Duo glared with bulging eyes and shouted at him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duo answered with a glare and a curse.

sentences.zh: 龍，榮之小字也。

translations.literal: Long was Rong’s childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: “Long” was Dong Rong’s pet name.
